## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
One defect needs fixing. `--json` takes the next argument as its path even when that argument is another flag, so `--json --junit <path>` fails to parse. That breaks the combination the description advertises ("alongside the required --junit destination"). No other defects were found in `app/cli.py` or `tests/test_cli.py`.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- app/cli.py:15 — correctness — When `--json` comes right before `--junit`, as in `parse_args(["--json", "--junit", "out.xml"])`, the parser stores `"--junit"` as the JSON path and then raises `ValueError("unknown option: out.xml")`. The `--json` branch only checks `i + 1 < len(args)` before consuming `args[i + 1]`. It lacks the `startswith("--")` check that the `--junit` branch uses on line 7. With `["--json", "--junit"]` it returns `{"json": "--junit"}` without an error, so `write_reports` creates a file named `--junit` and skips the required-path check for `--junit`. Fix it by applying the line-7 check here: use `args[i + 1]` and advance `i` only when the next argument exists and does not start with `--`. Then add a test for `["--json", "--junit", "x.xml"]` that expects `{"json": "results.json", "junit": "x.xml"}`. — Users who put `--json` before `--junit` get an "unknown option" error instead of both reports, or get a stray file named after the flag. The existing test only covers `--json` used alone or followed by a path, so it does not catch this.

(none)

## Strengths
- `tests/test_cli.py` checks that `--junit` with no path, and `--junit` followed by another flag, both raise `ValueError`. This guards the required-path rule that the reordering in `app/cli.py:7-10` must preserve.
